note_tweet.text:
YOUR SEO BOT KNOWS YOUR BUSINESS. NOW WHAT? 🎯

You gave Grok Bot your products, target customers, competitors, keywords, and business goals.

You researched the important unknowns.

You approved your SEO Business Brief.

Now it's time to turn that information into an actual plan.

But here's where many business owners make an expensive mistake.

They try to improve EVERYTHING at once.

Twenty SEO problems?

Twenty new tasks.

Ten competing websites?

Ten more audits.

And suddenly their AI is working nonstop without bringing in a single new customer.

Let's avoid that.

We're going to build a 30-DAY SEO ACTION PLAN that prioritizes the work most likely to bring your business qualified buyers.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🎯 STEP 1: START WITH THE MONEY

Not all search traffic has equal value.

Someone searching "what is email marketing?" may only want information.

Someone searching "email marketing automation service pricing" may be comparing services to buy.

Both searches matter.

But the second may be closer to generating revenue.

That's called BUYER INTENT.

Buyer intent means what someone wants to accomplish when searching.

Your SEO Lead should identify which searches are most relevant to people ready to buy your products or services.

For nonprofits, that might mean attracting potential donors, volunteers, or supporters.

For a plant-based business, that might mean helping people discover vegan products, coaching, restaurants, or services.

The goal isn't just more traffic.

It's more of the RIGHT traffic.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔎 STEP 2: FIND YOUR FASTEST SEO OPPORTUNITIES

Start with what your business already has.

Does your website have pages that appear in Google Search but receive few clicks?

Are important services missing from your website?

Do competing businesses answer buyer questions that your website ignores?

Does your homepage explain your offer clearly?

If your business qualifies for a Google Business Profile (GBP), are its categories, services, and business details accurate?

Your SEO Lead should identify these problems BEFORE recommending dozens of new pages.

Fixing a useful existing page may be a better first investment than creating ten new pages.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📋 STEP 3: COPY THIS PROMPT INTO YOUR SEO LEAD

Open the SEO Lead you created earlier.

Make sure your approved SEO Business Brief is available.

Then paste this prompt.

📌 COPY FROM HERE:

"You are my SEO Lead.

Your next assignment is to turn my approved SEO Business Brief into a practical, low-cost 30-DAY SEO ACTION PLAN.

Your goal is to help my business attract more qualified buyers through organic search.

Organic search means unpaid visits from search engines.

Use my approved Business Brief as your primary reference.

Do not repeat the entire business interview.

Do not launch a large competitor audit or open dozens of websites.

🎯 1. IDENTIFY MY BEST BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES

Review my business goals, products, services, competitors, and target buyers.

Identify which products or services are most important to promote.

Give priority to search terms that indicate buying interest.

Do not assume the keyword with the most searches has the highest business value.

If search-volume or ranking data is missing, label your ideas as research opportunities.

Do not invent data.

🔍 2. IDENTIFY MY THREE BIGGEST SEO PROBLEMS

Use verified information from my Business Brief.

Identify the three problems most likely to limit my search visibility, qualified leads, or sales.

Consider:

• Missing or unclear product and service pages.

• Weak website titles and descriptions.

• Poor internal linking between related pages.

• Important buyer questions my website doesn't answer.

• Relevant keywords competitors target that I may be missing.

• High-impression pages with low click-through rates, if verified data exists.

• Technical problems that prevent Google from accessing or indexing important pages.

• Incomplete Google Business Profile information, if my business qualifies.

Explain WHY each problem deserves attention.

📊 3. REVIEW MY EXISTING SEARCH PERFORMANCE

If Google Search Console data is available, use it.

Google Search Console is Google's free tool for understanding how a website performs in Google Search.

Review:

• Clicks: Visits from Google search results.

• Impressions: Times my website appeared in search results.

• CTR: Click-through rate, or the percentage of impressions that became clicks.

• Average position: The average ranking position reported by Google.

• Search queries: The words people searched for.

Look for valuable pages with high impressions but relatively few clicks.

Identify promising search queries where my website already has some visibility.

Prioritize pages that serve buyers with clear needs.

If Search Console is unavailable, explain how I can set it up or provide an export.

Do not invent a performance baseline.

📍 4. CHOOSE THE CORRECT SEO STRATEGY

Check my business type and Google Business Profile eligibility in my approved Business Brief.

If my business qualifies for GBP, consider:

• Primary and secondary business categories.

• Accurate products and services.

• Business description and attributes.

• Real customer reviews and helpful responses.

• Useful business photos and updates.

• Accurate service areas and public contact details.

If my business is online-only and ineligible, skip GBP optimization.

Instead, focus on website SEO, useful content, brand visibility, and appropriate online directories.

Never suggest fake offices, addresses, or service areas.

🏆 5. PRIORITIZE BY VALUE

Score each proposed SEO improvement using five factors:

Buyer value: Could this help attract customers who need my offer?

Evidence: Do we have real information supporting this improvement?

Expected impact: HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW.

Effort: How much time and work will this require?

Cost: Can I accomplish it using my existing tools and resources?

Prefer improvements with strong buyer value, reasonable evidence, and low cost.

Explain uncertainty.

Do not promise a specific Google ranking or revenue result.

🗓️ 6. BUILD MY 30-DAY ACTION PLAN

Organize the work into four weeks.

Use these themes as a starting point, but adjust the order to match my actual business needs.

WEEK 1: ESTABLISH THE BASELINE AND FIX CRITICAL PROBLEMS

Identify my three most important SEO opportunities.

Confirm whether Google Search Console is available.

Check whether my important website pages can be found and accessed.

Select one high-value page for immediate improvement.

If eligible, identify important GBP corrections.

WEEK 2: IMPROVE PAGES THAT CAN ATTRACT BUYERS

Improve titles, headings, and descriptions on high-priority pages.

Make the offer easier to understand.

Strengthen calls to action.

A call to action tells visitors what to do next.

Improve relevant internal links.

Prepare exact replacement copy for my approval.

WEEK 3: FILL IMPORTANT CONTENT AND TRUST GAPS

Identify unanswered buyer questions.

Improve one useful article, FAQ, product page, or service page.

Use real customer concerns and verified business information.

For eligible GBP businesses, recommend relevant service and review improvements.

Do not produce unnecessary or duplicate content.

WEEK 4: REVIEW RESULTS AND PLAN THE NEXT IMPROVEMENTS

Check completed tasks.

Review available search performance data.

Compare results with my starting baseline.

Explain which changes are too recent to judge.

Identify the next three priorities.

Prepare a simple monthly SEO report.

IMPORTANT:

Limit the initial schedule to ONE or TWO meaningful tasks per week.

Do not fill the calendar with busywork.

If a critical technical issue or major sales opportunity deserves immediate attention, move it to Week 1.

🛠️ 7. MAKE EVERY ACTION SPECIFIC

For each task, provide:

• The problem being solved.

• The specific page, keyword, or listing involved.

• Evidence supporting the problem.

• The exact action required.

• Expected impact.

• Estimated time and cost.

• Which Bot or human should handle the task.

• How I'll know the task is complete.

• Which result I should measure afterward.

If you recommend changing a page title, write the actual title.

If you recommend improving a headline, provide the replacement headline.

If you recommend adding an internal link, identify the source page and destination page.

If more research is required, say exactly what is missing.

📈 8. DEFINE HOW WE WILL MEASURE SUCCESS

Identify the most useful performance measures for my business.

Examples:

• Organic search clicks.

• Relevant search queries.

• Qualified leads.

• Booked appointments.

• Product purchases.

• Sales or donation conversions.

A conversion is when a visitor completes an important business action.

Use only verified measurements.

If lead or sales tracking doesn't exist, recommend a simple way to begin tracking.

Do not confuse higher traffic with higher revenue.

Explain that SEO improvements may take weeks or months to produce measurable search results.

💰 9. PROTECT MY WEEKLY GROK BOT USAGE

Do not create additional Bots.

Do not schedule Routines.

Do not repeatedly search the same websites.

Use information we already collected.

Suggest specialist Bots only when a specific task justifies one.

Keep your research focused.

Do not begin implementation without my approval.

📁 10. DELIVER MY COMPLETE PLAN

Create a document titled:

30-DAY SEO ACTION PLAN - [BUSINESS NAME]

Include:

• My primary SEO goal.

• My three biggest opportunities.

• A prioritized 30-day task table.

• A detailed Week 1 checklist.

• Recommended page improvements and draft copy.

• Expected time and cost.

• Performance measures.

• Missing information, if any.

• A short preview of possible priorities for Days 31–90.

🛑 11. STOP FOR MY APPROVAL

Present the completed plan.

Highlight the ONE task I should do first.

Explain why that task matters.

Wait for my approval before making changes, contacting people, scheduling Routines, or assigning work to other Bots.

Your job is to create a practical plan that helps my business grow.

Not a long list of tasks that only makes the Bots look busy."

✅ END OF PROMPT.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

✅ STEP 4: REVIEW YOUR 30-DAY ACTION PLAN

Your SEO Lead should now give you a prioritized task list.

Check that every task serves your business goals.

Look for specific actions rather than vague advice.

For example:

❌ "Improve your website SEO."

✅ "Rewrite the title and opening paragraph of your bookkeeping services page to explain who you serve, what you offer, and why buyers should choose you."

The second instruction gives you something you can actually finish.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 STEP 5: APPROVE YOUR FIRST ACTION

You now have:

✅ An approved SEO Business Brief.

✅ Three priority SEO opportunities.

✅ A 30-day action plan.

✅ A way to measure your progress.

You don't need to activate six Bots yet.

Start with the first approved task.

Let your SEO Lead complete one useful assignment.

Review the results.

Then move to the next task.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🚀 THE TAKEAWAY

SEO isn't about keeping your AI team busy.

It's about helping the right people find your business.

Your Bot's first job is to identify the work worth doing.

Its second job is to help you do that work correctly.

And its third job is to help you measure whether the work produced a useful result.

NEXT: Meet the specialist Grok Bots that can carry out your SEO Action Plan. 🤖

8/36

Grok Bot just got an update with v0.75.8! 🚀

Auto-review rule cards and smarter connectors
Also includes v0.75.6 and v0.75.7

Changelog v0.75.8

New:
• In the app, a Bot can offer to add, change, or remove one of your Auto-review rules on a card you confirm. Requires Grok Bot 0.75.2 or later.

Improved:
• Auto-review takes a second look before showing an approval card, so fewer safe actions need one.
• A Bot's status line shows up right after you send, even for quick replies.
• When background work finishes, the Bot completes what you asked, including steps you said to take once it was done, and says what it would do next instead of acting on its own or on another agent's approval. Requires Grok Bot 0.75.2 or later.
• Auto-review no longer counts a Bot saving or editing one of its routines as risky by itself.
• Auto-review approval cards in Slack describe the action, as they do in the app.
• Scheduling uses the calendar you've connected, Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar, and offers to connect one only when neither is.
• In a chat only you can see, a Bot reads your own private files without asking first.
• When a Bot installs a plugin while working, it can use the plugin's skills right away.
• People not on a Team Bot's share list, including teammates, no longer have access to it until an owner shares it with them. (Teams)

Fixed:
• When a connector such as X adds tools or fields, Bots can use them without you reconnecting it.
• A connector whose sign-in expired shows Authenticate in the app instead of Connected, matching what the Bot says. Requires Grok Bot 0.71.2 or later.
• Images a connector returns as files reach the Bot as images, and other binary files are no longer read as garbled text.
• X Money connects in one tap for more X accounts, and if it can't connect yours, the Bot says so instead of offering a sign-in.
• When a Bot posts to Slack for you, such as from a routine, your phone isn't notified and its unread badge doesn't go up.
• In Slack, when a safety check blocks a Bot's reply, the Bot says so and suggests trying a different message.
• For most accounts, with Route traffic through this computer on, the connection comes back as soon as the Bot's computer wakes.
• A Team Bot's routines can read Slack channels you and the Bot are both in, instead of refusing every read. (Teams)
• When a Team Bot edits one of its own Slack messages, the message shows a muted (edited) label. (Teams)
